Standard Text: Summarize agricultural, commercial, and technological developments during the Song Dynasties, and describe the role of Confucianism during the Song.
Chart Title: China's Population Boom During the Tang and Song Dynasties (600-1300 CE)

Data Source: Our World in Data population data (based on HYDE 3.3, Gapminder, and UN), long-run series for China
Citation: Our World in Data (2024), 'Population,' based on HYDE (2023), Gapminder (2022), and UN World Population Prospects (2022). Licensed CC BY 4.0.
Build Note: Supports the Song agricultural/commercial developments in 7.03. Filter the OWID long-run population series to China and the 600-1300 window.

Standard Text: Summarize agricultural, commercial, and technological developments during the Song Dynasties, and describe the role of Confucianism during the Song.
Chart Title: China's GDP per Capita in the Long Run: The Song Economic Peak

Data Source: Maddison Project Database 2020 (real GDP per capita, historical estimates for China)
Citation: Bolt, J. and van Zanden, J.L. (2020), 'Maddison Project Database, version 2020.' University of Groningen, GGDC. Licensed CC BY 4.0.

Standard Text: Examine the rise of the Mongol Empire, including the conquests of Genghis Khan.
Chart Title: Land Area of the Mongol Empire Compared to Other Great Empires at Their Peak
What the Chart Shows: Bar chart comparing the peak land area (in millions of square kilometers) of the Mongol Empire against the Umayyad Caliphate, Byzantine, Han, and Roman empires, with the Mongol Empire as the largest contiguous land empire.
Data Source: Taagepera, R. (1997), empire territorial-size estimates (millions of km^2 at peak)
Data Rights: Academic factual data (empire areas are facts, not copyrightable); cite source
Citation: Taagepera, R. (1997), 'Expansion and Contraction Patterns of Large Polities: Context for Russia,' International Studies Quarterly 41(3): 475-504.
Build Note: Supports the rise of the Mongol Empire (7.04/7.05). Taagepera's figures are widely cited historian estimates; label as estimates. Same source underpins the Byzantine and Ottoman charts below.

Standard Text: Identify the continuation of the Eastern Roman Empire as the Byzantine Empire, and describe the diffusion of Christianity and the Latin language.
Chart Title: The Long Decline of the Byzantine Empire's Territory, 550-1450 CE

Data Source: Taagepera, R. (1997), Byzantine (Eastern Roman) territorial-size estimates over time
Data Rights: Academic factual data (empire areas are facts, not copyrightable); cite source
Citation: Taagepera, R. (1997), 'Expansion and Contraction Patterns of Large Polities: Context for Russia,' International Studies Quarterly 41(3): 475-504.
Build Note: Supports 7.12-7.14 (Byzantine continuity, Justinian, and geography). Pairs naturally with the Ottoman-growth chart to show the transfer of power in 1453.

Standard Text: Explain how the location of the Italian Peninsula impacted the movement of resources, knowledge, and culture throughout Italy's independent trade cities.
Chart Title: Renaissance Italy's GDP per Capita Compared to the Rest of Europe

Data Source: Maddison Project Database 2020 (real GDP per capita for Italy and other European economies, 1300-1600)
Citation: Bolt, J. and van Zanden, J.L. (2020), 'Maddison Project Database, version 2020.' University of Groningen, GGDC. Licensed CC BY 4.0.

Standard Text: Analyze Johannes Gutenberg's printing press and William Tyndale's translation of the Bible into the English language as vehicles for the spread of books, growth of literacy, and dissemination of knowledge.
Chart Title: Explosion of Book Production in Europe After the Printing Press

Data Source: Buringh, E. & van Zanden, J.L. (2009), manuscript and printed-book production in Europe by century, republished by Our World in Data

Standard Text: Identify the significance of the voyages and routes of discovery of the following explorers by their sponsoring country: • England: Henry Hudson • France: Jacques Cartier • Portugal: Vasco da Gama, Bartolomeu Dias • Spain: Christopher Columbus, Hernando de Soto, Ferdinand Magellan, Amerigo Vespucci
Chart Title: Timeline of the Major Voyages of the Age of Exploration (1487-1610)
What the Chart Shows: Horizontal timeline plotting the major exploration voyages from Bartolomeu Dias (1488) through Henry Hudson (1609-10), color-coded by sponsoring country (Portugal, Spain, France, England).
Data Source: Documented voyage dates by explorer and sponsoring country (Dias 1488, Columbus 1492, Vespucci 1499, da Gama 1498, Cabral 1500, Magellan 1519-22, Cartier 1534, de Soto 1539, Hudson 1609-10)
Data Rights: Public Domain (verifiable historical dates, not copyrightable)
Citation: Voyage dates compiled from established public-domain historical record; see Library of Congress, 'Exploring the Early Americas.'
Build Note: Supports 7.59 (voyages and routes by sponsoring country). This is a curated timeline of verifiable, public-domain dated events rather than a statistical dataset; no numbers are invented. Each date should be double-checked against a reference before publishing.

Standard Text: Explain the impact of the Columbian Exchange on people, plants, animals, technology, culture, ideas, and diseases among Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Americas in the 15th and 16th centuries, and examine the major economic and social effects on each continent.
Chart Title: The Great Dying: Collapse of the Indigenous American Population After 1492
What the Chart Shows: Line chart of the estimated Indigenous population of the Americas dropping from roughly 60 million in 1492 to about 6 million by 1600, driven largely by Old World diseases in the Columbian Exchange.

Data Rights: CC BY — Our World in Data
Citation: Koch, A., Brierley, C., Maslin, M.M., Lewis, S.L. (2019), 'Earth system impacts of the European arrival and Great Dying in the Americas after 1492,' Quaternary Science Reviews 207: 13-36. Licensed CC BY 4.0.
Build Note: Supports 7.64 (Columbian Exchange, especially disease and the major demographic/social effects on the Americas). Peer-reviewed, CC BY, with data in the supplement.
